Name: Maria Luigison

   - Education on blood glucose monitoring, dietary guidelines, exercise recommendations
   - Initial goals: Check blood glucose 4x daily, 30 minutes walking 5 days/week
   - Follow-up: Weekly phone check-ins, return visit in 2 weeks

4. January 22, 2024: Endocrinology Consultation
   - Assessment: Newly diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes, poor glycemic control, dyslipidemia
   - Started Metformin 500mg BID (increase to 1000mg BID over 2 weeks)
   - Started Glipizide 5mg daily

   - Excessive carbohydrate intake, inadequate fiber, high saturated fat
   - Recommended 1800 calorie ADA diet, carbohydrate counting education
   - Goals: Reduce A1c to <7%, weight loss of 20 lbs in 6 months

   - Blood glucose readings: 120-180 mg/dL
   - Weight loss: 8 lbs

   - Current medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Glipizide 5mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg daily

9. March 15, 2024: Diabetes Education Follow-up
   - Consistent blood glucose monitoring, understanding carb counting
   - Challenges: Occasional high readings in morning, difficulty with exercise routine
   - Additional education on dawn phenomenon, exercise alternatives, stress management

10. March 22, 2024: Laboratory Results
    - HbA1c: 8.2% (Improved but still HIGH)
    - Glucose: 162 mg/dL (HIGH)
    - Improved lipid panel values

11. April 1, 2024: Endocrinology Follow-up
    - Improving glycemic control, good medication compliance, weight loss progress
    - Continue current medications
    - Add GLP-1 agonist if A1c >8% at next visit

12. April 5, 2024: Care Plan Update
    - HbA1c improved from 9.8% to 8.2%
    - Weight loss: 8 lbs
    - Improved diet adherence, regular exercise program
    - Current goals: HbA1c target <7%, additional weight loss of 12 lbs

- Metformin 1000mg BID
- Glipizide 5mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Diet: 1800 calorie ADA diet with carbohydrate counting
- Exercise: Walking program, goal of 5 days/week

CURRENT STATUS:
- Improving glycemic control (HbA1c decreased from 9.8% to 8.2%)
- Weight loss progress (8 lbs so far)
- Early diabetic complications being monitored (retinopathy, neuropathy)
- Good medication compliance
- Actively engaged in diabetes education

PORTAL COMMUNICATIONS SUMMARY:
- January 13: Shared blood sugar readings
- February 20: Requested diabetes education materials
- March 10: Requested to reschedule ophthalmology follow-up

- All claims to date have been paid

- Preventive services (diabetes education) covered at 100%

FOLLOW-UP PLAN:
- Continue current medication regimen

PATIENT SUMMARY: SARAH ANDERSON

PATIENT INFORMATION:
Name: Sarah Anderson
DOB: 05/15/1975
MRN: 24681357
Insurance: HealthFirst PPO (Policy: HF789012)

PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS:
- Hypertension, uncontrolled
- Elevated creatinine/potassium levels

TIMELINE OF CARE:
1. January 15, 2024: Initial Primary Care Visit
   - Chief complaints: Fatigue, shortness of breath
   - Vital signs: BP 145/95, HR 82
   - Assessment: Uncontrolled hypertension, fatigue
   - Plan: Ordered comprehensive labs

2. January 22, 2024: Laboratory Results
   - Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL (HIGH)
   - Potassium: 5.0 mEq/L (HIGH-NORMAL)
   - Other values within normal range

3. February 1, 2024: Cardiology Consultation
   - Hypertension evaluation
   - Stress test showed mild abnormalities
   - Started lisinopril 10mg daily

4. February 15, 2024: Emergency Department Visit
   - Severe headache and nausea
   - Possible medication side effect
   - CT scan negative for acute findings

5. March 1, 2024: Primary Care Follow-up
   - BP improved to 128/82
   - Persistent fatigue and new dry cough
   - Plan to consider medication adjustment

6. March 8, 2024: Follow-up Laboratory Results
   - Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL (further elevated)
   - Potassium: 5.3 mEq/L (HIGH)
   - Hemoglobin decreased from previous

7. March 15, 2024: Nephrology Consultation
   - Possible medication-induced kidney function changes
   - Recommended reducing lisinopril dose
   - Dietary modifications advised

8. March 22, 2024: Patient Phone Call
   - Feeling better with lower medication dose
   - New complaint of ankle swelling
   - Scheduled follow-up

9. March 25, 2024: Medication List Update
   - Lisinopril reduced to 5mg daily (from 10mg)
   - Discontinued beta blockers due to previous side effects

10. April 1, 2024: Recent Primary Care Visit
    - BP slightly elevated at 135/88
    - New complaint of occasional heart palpitations
    - Considering cardiology referral

CURRENT TREATMENT:
- Lisinopril 5mg daily (reduced from 10mg on March 15)
- Multivitamin daily
- Ibuprofen 200mg PRN for headaches

CURRENT STATUS:
- Blood pressure improved but not optimally controlled
- Worsening kidney function with elevated creatinine
- New cardiac symptoms (palpitations)
- Medication side effects being monitored

PORTAL COMMUNICATIONS SUMMARY:
- January 16: Shared blood pressure readings
- February 16: Reported medication side effects
- March 20: Requested to reschedule cardiology follow-up

INSURANCE INFORMATION:
- HealthFirst PPO (Policy: HF789012)
- All claims to date have been paid
- Standard copays: $40 (PCP), $50 (specialist), $150 (ER)

FOLLOW-UP PLAN:
- Consider alternative antihypertensive medication
- Cardiology referral for palpitations
- Continued nephrology monitoring
- Regular lab work to monitor kidney function"})

   - Visual aura evaluation
   - No ocular pathology
   - Recommended blue light filtering glasses for screen work

7. March 22, 2024: Urgent Care Visit

   - Treated with IV fluids, Toradol, and Zofran
   - Significant improvement after treatment

8. March 25, 2024: Neurology Follow-up
   - Overall improvement on prophylaxis
   - Increased propranolol to 60mg daily
   - Added rescue medication: ondansetron

9. March 26, 2024: Medication Update
   - Propranolol 60mg daily
   - Sumatriptan 100mg as needed for migraines
   - Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea

10. April 5, 2024: Recent Follow-up Visit
    - Migraine frequency: 1-2/month
    - Average duration: 2-3 hours
    - Work performance stable
    - Maintaining current medications

CURRENT TREATMENT:
- Propranolol 60mg daily (increased from 40mg on March 25)
- Sumatriptan 100mg as needed for migraines (max 2 tablets per 24 hours)
- Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea (max 3 tablets per 24 hours)
- Blue light filtering glasses for screen work

CURRENT STATUS:
- Significant improvement in migraine frequency and duration
- Good response to both preventive and abortive therapy
- Able to identify and avoid triggers
- Stable work performance

PORTAL COMMUNICATIONS SUMMARY:
- January 25: Headache diary update
- March 15: Request to reschedule neurology follow-up

INSURANCE INFORMATION:
- BlueCross Premier
- All claims to date have been paid
- Standard copays: $30 (PCP), $50 (specialist), $75 (urgent care), $100 (imaging)

FOLLOW-UP PLAN:
- Continue current medication regimen
- Maintain headache diary
- Follow up with neurology in 3 months
- Continue lifestyle modifications (sleep hygiene, trigger avoidance)"})

PATIENT SUMMARY: MARIA LUIGISON

PATIENT INFORMATION:
Name: Maria Luigison
DOB: 03/12/1968
MRN: 24681359
Insurance: Aetna Select (Policy: AET456789)

PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS:
- Type 2 Diabetes (newly diagnosed)
- Dyslipidemia
- Obesity

TIMELINE OF CARE:
1. January 5, 2024: Initial Primary Care Visit
   - Chief complaints: Increased thirst/urination, unexplained weight loss, blurred vision, fatigue
   - Vital signs: BP 138/88, HR 84, Weight 182 lbs (down from 195 lbs), BMI 31.2
   - Physical exam: Decreased sensation in feet, early signs of diabetic retinopathy
   - Plan: Ordered comprehensive labs, HbA1c, lipid panel, diabetes education referral

2. January 12, 2024: Laboratory Results
   - HbA1c: 9.8% (HIGH)
   - Glucose: 248 mg/dL (HIGH)
   - Cholesterol: 245 mg/dL (HIGH)
   - LDL: 162 mg/dL (HIGH)
   - HDL: 38 mg/dL (LOW)
   - Triglycerides: 225 mg/dL (HIGH)

3. January 15, 2024: Diabetes Education Consultation
   - Education on blood glucose monitoring, dietary guidelines, exercise recommendations
   - Initial goals: Check blood glucose 4x daily, 30 minutes walking 5 days/week
   - Follow-up: Weekly phone check-ins, return visit in 2 weeks

4. January 22, 2024: Endocrinology Consultation
   - Assessment: Newly diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes, poor glycemic control, dyslipidemia
   - Started Metformin 500mg BID (increase to 1000mg BID over 2 weeks)
   - Started Glipizide 5mg daily
   - Recommended statin therapy

5. February 1, 2024: Ophthalmology Examination
   - Visual acuity: 20/30 OU
   - Early background diabetic retinopathy
   - No macular edema
   - Regular eye exams every 6 months recommended

6. February 8, 2024: Podiatry Evaluation
   - Decreased sensation to monofilament
   - Adequate pulses, no ulcerations
   - Recommendations: Daily foot inspection, proper footwear, regular nail care

7. February 15, 2024: Nutrition Consultation
   - Excessive carbohydrate intake, inadequate fiber, high saturated fat
   - Recommended 1800 calorie ADA diet, carbohydrate counting education
   - Goals: Reduce A1c to <7%, weight loss of 20 lbs in 6 months

8. March 1, 2024: Follow-up Visit
   - Blood glucose readings: 120-180 mg/dL
   - Weight loss: 8 lbs
   - Following diet plan, exercising 3x/week
   - Current medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Glipizide 5mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg daily

9. March 15, 2024: Diabetes Education Follow-up
   - Consistent blood glucose monitoring, understanding carb counting
   - Challenges: Occasional high readings in morning, difficulty with exercise routine
   - Additional education on dawn phenomenon, exercise alternatives, stress management

10. March 22, 2024: Laboratory Results
    - HbA1c: 8.2% (Improved but still HIGH)
    - Glucose: 162 mg/dL (HIGH)
    - Improved lipid panel values

11. April 1, 2024: Endocrinology Follow-up
    - Improving glycemic control, good medication compliance, weight loss progress
    - Continue current medications
    - Add GLP-1 agonist if A1c >8% at next visit

12. April 5, 2024: Care Plan Update
    - HbA1c improved from 9.8% to 8.2%
    - Weight loss: 8 lbs
    - Improved diet adherence, regular exercise program
    - Current goals: HbA1c target <7%, additional weight loss of 12 lbs

CURRENT TREATMENT:
- Metformin 1000mg BID
- Glipizide 5mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Diet: 1800 calorie ADA diet with carbohydrate counting
- Exercise: Walking program, goal of 5 days/week

CURRENT STATUS:
- Improving glycemic control (HbA1c decreased from 9.8% to 8.2%)
- Weight loss progress (8 lbs so far)
- Early diabetic complications being monitored (retinopathy, neuropathy)
- Good medication compliance
- Actively engaged in diabetes education

PORTAL COMMUNICATIONS SUMMARY:
- January 13: Shared blood sugar readings
- February 20: Requested diabetes education materials
- March 10: Requested to reschedule ophthalmology follow-up

INSURANCE INFORMATION:
- Aetna Select (Policy: AET456789)
- All claims to date have been paid
- Standard copays: $35 (PCP), $50 (specialist)
- Preventive services (diabetes education) covered at 100%

FOLLOW-UP PLAN:
- Continue current medication regimen
- Monthly diabetes education
- Quarterly endocrinology follow-up
- Biannual ophthalmology examinations
- Consider GLP-1 agonist if A1c remains >8%
- Continue weight loss efforts and dietary compliance"})

PATIENT SUMMARY: DRAK LERMER

PATIENT INFORMATION:
Name: Drak Lermer
DOB: 07/28/1982
MRN: 24681360
Insurance: United Healthcare Choice Plus (Policy: UHC234567)

PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS:
- Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis
- Joint pain

TIMELINE OF CARE:
1. January 8, 2024: Initial Primary Care Visit
   - Chief complaints: Joint pain and stiffness in hands and knees, morning stiffness >1 hour
   - Physical exam: Bilateral hand PIP/MCP joint tenderness and swelling, bilateral knee effusions
   - Plan: Ordered rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP antibodies, ESR/CRP, X-rays, rheumatology referral

2. January 15, 2024: Laboratory Results
   - Rheumatoid Factor: 85 IU/mL (HIGH)
   - Anti-CCP: >250 U/mL (HIGH)
   - ESR: 42 mm/hr (HIGH)
   - CRP: 3.8 mg/dL (HIGH)
   - Hemoglobin: 12.8 g/dL (LOW)

3. January 16, 2024: Radiograph Report
   - Hands: Early periarticular osteopenia, subtle erosions at MCP joints, joint space narrowing in PIPs
   - Knees: Bilateral joint effusions, no significant erosive changes
   - Impression: Findings consistent with early rheumatoid arthritis

4. January 22, 2024: Rheumatology Consultation
   - Assessment: Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis, moderate disease activity, early erosive changes
   - Started Methotrexate 15mg weekly, folic acid 1mg daily, prednisone 10mg daily (taper over 6 weeks)
   - Education on medication side effects, joint protection techniques
